segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And well, when the technical problem started, Mr. Ford was apologizing and said, hey, look, I'm sorry.
segments.zh: 好吧，当技术问题开始时，福特先生正在道歉并说，嘿，看，对不起。

segments.en: And he also used this interesting phrase, bear with me.
segments.zh: 他也用了这个有趣的短语，忍受我。

segments.en: Bear with me a second.
segments.zh: 忍受我一秒钟。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So this is interesting because it's not the animal, the bear.
segments.zh: 所以这很有趣，因为它不是动物，不是熊。

segments.en: Right, right.
segments.zh: 对，对。

segments.en: This is different.
segments.zh: 这是不同的。

segments.en: It's more like, excuse me, please be patient.
segments.zh: 更像，对不起，请耐心等待。

segments.en: I have to do something and you have to wait.
segments.zh: 我必须做点什么，你必须等待。

segments.en: So this is a very, very polite way of asking some people or some person to wait for you.
segments.zh: 所以这是一种非常非常有礼貌的方式，要求一些人或某个人等你。

segments.en: To tolerate.
segments.zh: 容忍。

segments.en: Yes.
segments.zh: 是的。

segments.en: So both the animal bear and to bear with me are spelled the same way.
segments.zh: 因此，动物熊和与我一起承受的拼写方式相同。

segments.en: It looks exactly like the animal, but we're not talking about the animal.
segments.zh: 它看起来和动物一模一样，但我们不是在谈论动物。

segments.en: No, we're asking someone to tolerate something that's annoying or frustrating.
segments.zh: 不，我们要求某人容忍烦人或令人沮丧的事情。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: For example, I'm trying to show you a file on my computer, Marco.
segments.zh: 例如，我试图在我的计算机上向您显示一个文件，Marco。

segments.en: My computer's not working.
segments.zh: 我的电脑不工作。

segments.en: I say, please bear with me a second.
segments.zh: 我说，请耐心等待。

segments.en: I have to reboot my computer.
segments.zh: 我必须重新启动我的电脑。

segments.en: I have to wait here.
segments.zh: 我必须在这里等。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: Now, towards the end of the dialogue, when we talked about to crop up, the second part of that, Mr. Ford said, unfortunately, technical problems do crop up from time to time.
segments.zh: 现在，在对话快结束时，当我们谈论要出现的第二部分时，福特先生说，不幸的是，技术问题确实时不时出现。

segments.en: So we already discussed cropped up.
segments.zh: 所以我们已经讨论过了。

segments.en: What is time to time?
segments.zh: 什么是时间？

segments.en: From time to time.
segments.zh: 时不时。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So that's a set phrase because we said already that you could also say sometimes.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个固定的短语，因为我们已经说过你有时也可以说。

segments.en: So from time to time means every once in a while or occasionally.
segments.zh: 所以不时意味着偶尔或偶尔。

segments.en: So it's an adverbial phrase.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个副词短语。

segments.en: It's a way of telling people how often something happens, but in this case, it's not very common.
segments.zh: 这是一种告诉人们某事发生频率的方式，但在这种情况下，这并不常见。

segments.en: So for example, you can say, I like to go to the movies from time to time.
segments.zh: 例如，你可以说，我喜欢不时去看电影。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So maybe once or twice a month, you like to go to the movies.
segments.zh: 所以也许一个月一次或两次，你喜欢去看电影。

segments.en: But what if I come to work every day?
segments.zh: 但是如果我每天都来上班怎么办？

segments.en: Do I come to work from time to time?
segments.zh: 我会不时来上班吗？

segments.en: No.
segments.zh: 不。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So from time to time is rarely or occasionally, not very often.
segments.zh: 所以不时很少或偶尔，不经常。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: So now let's listen to our dialogue one last time and review everything we've just learned.
segments.zh: 所以现在让我们最后一次听我们的对话，回顾我们刚刚学到的一切。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So if we could dim the lights, Jonathan, we can kick off with the first TV advert.
segments.zh: 因此，如果我们可以调暗灯光，乔纳森，我们可以从第一个电视广告开始。

segments.en: Please note that we're still in the early days with this advert, so it might seem a bit rough around the edges.
segments.zh: 请注意，我们仍处于使用此广告的早期阶段，因此边缘可能看起来有点粗糙。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So I just need to click this and the advert should pop up on the screen.
segments.zh: 所以我只需要点击这个，广告应该会在屏幕上弹出。

segments.en: Hmm.
segments.zh: 嗯。

segments.en: Sorry about this.
segments.zh: 对不起这个。

segments.en: Bear with me a second.
segments.zh: 忍受我一秒钟。

segments.en: There seems to be a problem with the projector.
segments.zh: 投影机似乎有问题。

segments.en: Let me see.
segments.zh: 让我看看。

segments.en: Jonathan, could you lend a hand a second?
segments.zh: 乔纳森，能过来帮一下忙吗？

segments.en: It looks like the projector is not recognizing the computer.
segments.zh: 看起来投影仪无法识别计算机。

segments.en: Let me check the connection a second.
segments.zh: 让我检查一下连接。

segments.en: Well, the connection seems okay and the computer is running normally.
segments.zh: 好吧，连接似乎正常，计算机运行正常。

segments.en: Hmm.
segments.zh: 嗯。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Sorry, guys.
segments.zh: 对不起，伙计们。

segments.en: Obviously a problem with the system.
segments.zh: 显然是系统的问题。

segments.en: Let's just reboot and start over.
segments.zh: 让我们重新启动并重新开始。

segments.en: Let's see if this resolves the issue.
segments.zh: 让我们看看这是否解决了这个问题。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Let's try again.
segments.zh: 让我们再试一次。

segments.en: No, still nothing, Michael.
segments.zh: 不，仍然没有，迈克尔。

segments.en: There might be a technical issue with the projector.
segments.zh: 投影机可能存在技术问题。

segments.en: I think maybe the projector has overheated.
segments.zh: 我想可能投影仪过热了。

segments.en: We might need to cool it down for 10 minutes and start again.
segments.zh: 我们可能需要冷却 10 分钟并重新开始。

segments.en: I'll call IT support to come over right now.
segments.zh: 我马上叫 IT 技术支持过来。

segments.en: Okay, guys.
segments.zh: 好吧，伙计们。

segments.en: Unfortunately, technical problems do crop up from time to time, don't they?
segments.zh: 不幸的是，技术问题会不时出现，不是吗？

segments.en: But it's not a huge problem.
segments.zh: 但这不是一个大问题。

segments.en: In the meantime, while the IT guys get to work on that, I can talk a little bit more about the advertising concept and what we're looking to achieve overall with this campaign.
segments.zh: 与此同时，当 IT 人员开始努力时，我可以更多地谈论广告概念以及我们希望通过这个活动获得整体目标。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So this was part seven of our presentation series.
segments.zh: 所以这是我们演讲系列的第七部分。

segments.en: And actually, these type of problems occur very, very often, specifically with the laptop and the projector.
segments.zh: 实际上，这些类型的问题经常发生，特别是在笔记本电脑和投影仪上。

segments.en: And sometimes it doesn't work.
segments.zh: 有时它不起作用。

segments.en: It doesn't recognize it.
segments.zh: 它不认识它。

segments.en: And so this is a nice way of handling it.
segments.zh: 所以这是一种很好的处理方式。

segments.en: This is.
segments.zh: 这是。

segments.en: And we hope that these are phrases that you can use in your daily life as well.
segments.zh: 我们希望这些短语也可以在您的日常生活中使用。

segments.en: Maybe you're working with your colleagues and you're having some technical problems.
segments.zh: 也许您正在与您的同事一起工作，并且您遇到了一些技术问题。

segments.en: Or if you're having a problem and someone gives you instructions for how to solve that problem.
segments.zh: 或者，如果您遇到问题并且有人为您提供如何解决该问题的说明。

segments.en: Like, I often get this from my technical team.
segments.zh: 就像，我经常从我的技术团队那里得到这个。

segments.en: I say, listen, I have a problem.
segments.zh: 我说，听着，我有问题。

segments.en: And they say, hey, just reboot your computer and it will be okay.
segments.zh: 他们说，嘿，只需重新启动您的计算机，就可以了。

segments.en: So these are very, very common issues that I think that you can learn how to describe in English with today's lesson.
segments.zh: 所以这些都是非常非常常见的问题，我认为您可以通过今天的课程学习如何用英语来描述。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: And of course, if you guys have any questions or any doubts about this or any of our lessons, please come to our website EnglishPod.com.
segments.zh: 当然，如果你们对本课程或我们的任何课程有任何疑问或疑问，请访问我们的网站 englishpod.com。

segments.en: On the lessons page, you can leave your comments and questions.
segments.zh: 在课程页面上，您可以留下您的评论和问题。

segments.en: And we'll see you guys next time.
segments.zh: 我们下次再见。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。
